description: Police no longer make sure you exchange insurance at a Georgia wreck. Storage charges mount while you wait for the report. What to get at the scene.
shortAnswer: Always get that information yourself at the scene if you possibly can. In my experience, police officers will not give that information to you. Clients wait three to five days for the wreck report while storage charges on the towed car are mounting.

sections.heading: What Georgia law says
sections.shortAnswer: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273.1 says the officer at the scene “shall instruct” each driver to report names, the license number, and the name of the liability insurance carrier. It does not make the officer collect the information and hand it to you.

sections.heading: Why the wait causes so much trouble
sections.shortAnswer: The City of Atlanta says its police reports are available within 5 to 7 business days. Norcross says 3 to 5 business days. The wrecker’s daily storage charges keep adding up.

sections.heading: When your child is the one who was hurt
sections.shortAnswer: If your child is hurt, your child comes first. Ask a spouse, a friend, or a bystander to photograph the other car and its tag, and ask the officer where your car is going.

sections.heading: What to get at the scene
sections.shortAnswer: Photograph the other driver’s insurance card, front and back, the driver’s license, and the tag on every vehicle involved. Write down the officer’s name, the agency, and the report number.

sections.heading: If you already left without it
sections.shortAnswer: Report the wreck to your own insurance company right away. Look at your own policy. Find your car and call the wrecker. Keep every receipt.

sections.heading: What I tell parents to do today
sections.shortAnswer: Put a copy of your insurance card in every car, and a picture of it on your phone. Teach your teenager the list, and practice it.

faq.q: Will the police give me the other driver's insurance information after a wreck in Georgia?
faq.a: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273.1 says the officer at the scene “shall instruct” each driver to report the name of the liability insurance carrier. It does not make the officer collect the information and hand it to you. In my experience, they will not give that information to you.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a police report after a wreck in Georgia?
faq.a: The City of Atlanta says its police reports are available within 5 to 7 business days. Norcross says 3 to 5 business days. Any person whose name or identifying information is in the report may get a copy, personally or through a lawyer.

faq.q: What if my child is hurt and I leave the wreck in the ambulance?
faq.a: If your child is hurt, your child comes first. Hand the job to someone else. Ask a spouse, a friend, or a bystander to photograph the other car and its tag, and ask the officer where your car is going.

faq.q: Can I get my child's car seat and belongings out of a towed car in Georgia?
faq.a: A towing and storage firm must allow the owner to retrieve personal property in a stored vehicle for up to 30 days from the date its notice was sent. The statute does not cover items attached or affixed to the vehicle. Ask for the car seat anyway, and ask early.
